title: Break the remaining seven contracts and confirm each fails
description:
FROM THE i0o REVIEW, which reported an honest partial rather than a confident pass. Its verdict: item 1 of its brief — "does drift actually fail?" — is verified for only 2 of 9 contracts. The other 7 were confirmed to have genuine two-sided readers (no orphan fixtures) but were never individually broken and confirmed red.

That gap is the whole epic. A contract nobody has SEEN fail is a comment with extra steps, and this epic exists because a comment saying "mirrored from load.go" kept both suites green through a one-sided edit. Seven contracts currently rest on the same kind of assumption the epic was created to remove.

ALREADY DONE, do not redo: collect-vocabulary.json (the DONE_WITH_CONCERNS/DONE alternation, Go side) and runners-config-contract.json (max_length 512 -> 511 in internal/herd/config/load.go, one-sided Go edit, contract untouched — TestSandboxImageValuesMatchContract went red naming both the length and the refusal message).

THE SEVEN, with their readers as the review mapped them:
  signal-source-cases.json       Go internal/herd/config/signal_parity_test.go        TS cloud/factory/test/webhook-sources.test.ts
  sweep-policy-cases.json        Go internal/herd/config/sweep_parity_test.go         TS cloud/factory/test/sweep-contract.test.ts
  sweep-selection-contract.json  Go internal/herd/config/sweep_parity_test.go AND internal/tick/sweep_selection_parity_test.go   TS cloud/factory/test/sweep-contract.test.ts
  sandbox-image-cases.json       Go internal/sandbox/image_parity_test.go             TS cloud/factory/test/repo-config.test.ts
  worker-boot-contract.json      Go internal/sandbox/worker_parity_test.go            TS cloud/factory/test/worker-boot.test.ts
  message-context.json           Go internal/operator/message_context_parity_test.go  TS cloud/factory/test/message-context.test.ts
  tracker-layout.json            Go internal/tick/tracker_layout_parity_test.go       TS cloud/factory/test/tick-membership.test.ts

METHOD, and the shape matters. For each contract, make a ONE-SIDED edit to an IMPLEMENTATION — never to the contract file — and confirm the corresponding suite goes red. Then revert and confirm green. Do it for the Go side AND the TS side separately: a contract that fails on a Go edit but not a TS edit is only half a contract, and the TS half is the one that leaves the repo at extraction. sweep-selection-contract.json has TWO Go readers; break it in a way that exercises both, or break it twice.

Editing the CONTRACT FILE is the wrong experiment — that changes what both sides are compared against, so both go red for the trivial reason. The experiment that matters is one implementation drifting away from an unchanged contract, because that is what actually happens.

Report per contract: the exact edit, the failing test name, the failure text, and confirmation of green after revert. Where a contract turns out NOT to fail on a one-sided edit, that is the most valuable finding in the tick — say so loudly and do not fix it silently.

NOTE: the previous attempt at this sweep was delegated to a background agent that stalled after 600s and was abandoned. Do this work directly in your own worktree rather than delegating it.

acceptance_criteria: All seven contracts are individually break-tested on BOTH the Go and the TS side by a one-sided implementation edit with the contract file unchanged, each with the failing test name and failure text recorded, and each reverted to green. sweep-selection-contract.json exercises both of its Go readers. Any contract that does NOT fail on a one-sided edit is reported prominently rather than fixed silently. go test ./... and the factory vitest suite green at the end.
